Introduction to geno2ped

Source: vignettes/geno2ped-intro.Rmd
geno2ped-intro.Rmd

Overview

geno2ped is an R package for rapid pedigree construction from SNP genotype data. It infers parent-offspring relationships using genomic similarity and Mendelian error validation, and supports PLINK, VCF, and CSV input formats.

Installation 

devtools::install_github("ampofoissabel-quangen/geno2ped")

Loading the Package 

library(geno2ped)
#> Warning: replacing previous import 'S4Arrays::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' by
#> 'DelayedArray::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' when loading 'SummarizedExperiment'

Reading Genotypes

From a CSV file

The simplest input format is a CSV where the first column contains sample IDs and the remaining columns contain SNP genotypes (0/1/2):

geno <- read_genotypes(
  csv             = "path/to/genotypes.csv",
  sample_metadata = "path/to/metadata.csv"
)

From PLINK files 

geno <- read_genotypes(
  bed_prefix      = "path/to/mydata",
  sample_metadata = "path/to/metadata.csv"
)

From VCF files 

geno <- read_genotypes(
  vcf             = "path/to/mydata.vcf.gz",
  sample_metadata = "path/to/metadata.csv"
)

The genotype object

read_genotypes() returns a list with four elements:

Element Description
$G Genotype matrix (samples x SNPs, 0/1/2)
$ids Sample ID vector
$map SNP map (chr, pos, snp)
$meta Sample metadata (ID, Sex, BirthYear)

Sample metadata format

Your metadata CSV should look like this:

ID Sex BirthYear
Sample001 M 1985
Sample002 F 1990
Sample003 M 2005

Building a Pedigree

Using a preset

The easiest way is to use a built-in preset:

res <- build_pedigree(
  geno,
  preset  = "high_precision",
  verbose = TRUE
)

Three presets are available:

Preset Use case
none Manual threshold control
high_precision Minimise false positives
high_coverage Maximise assignments

Custom thresholds 

res <- build_pedigree(
  geno,
  s_threshold    = 0.75,
  me_max         = 0.003,
  oh_max         = 20,
  use_sex        = TRUE,
  use_age        = TRUE,
  min_parent_gap = 2,
  top_k          = 3
)

The result object

build_pedigree() returns a list with:

Element Description
$pedigree Final pedigree (ID, Sire, Dam, status)
$assignments All candidate parent scores
$trios Best trio per offspring
$trios_all All evaluated trios
$summary Assignment statistics
$settings Parameters used

Viewing results 

# View the pedigree
res$pedigree

# View summary statistics
res$summary

Visualising Results 

# Similarity score distribution
plot_kinship(res)

# Mendelian error rate distribution
plot_me(res)

# Assignment outcome counts
plot_assignment_status(res)

Saving Results 

write_outputs(
  res,
  outdir = "geno2ped_results",
  prefix = "my_run"
)

This creates the following files in geno2ped_results/:

  • my_run_pedigree.csv — final pedigree
  • my_run_assignments.csv — candidate scores
  • my_run_trios.csv — best trios
  • my_run_summary.txt — run statistics
  • my_run_settings.txt — parameters used
